title: The Lang–Plaut problem
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's negative answer (2026) to the question of Lang and Plaut: a subset of Hilbert space with doubling constant at most 76800 that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional Euclidean or normed space. The first lesson proves the packing lemma, the doubling of Euclidean subsets, and constructs the set from coloured strips at scales 1000^-j with its doubling bound. The second collects good points and line integrals of Lipschitz maps of plane domains and the lexicographic maximum of the squared derivative columns of all sheets. The third proves the two energy estimates near that maximum. The fourth chooses lines of small energy, compares offsets at crossings, and derives a packing contradiction.
prerequisites: core course Measure and Integration (Fremlin, Measure Theory: Volume 1, 134A; Volume 2, 225E, 251N, 252B, 252D, 261E, 262B, 262Q, 263A)
core course Real Analysis II (compactness of the unit sphere of R^k, minima of continuous functions)
